title: How Do You Integrate Off-page Signals into Your AI Visibility Strategy?
summary: Off-page signals are often the primary source for AI answer engines. Here's how to leverage them.
body_text: Key Takeaways Off-page signals are often the primary source for AI answer engines, with Reddit alone accounting for 21.9% of all off-page citations across every AI model tracked, more than double the next closest source, YouTube, at 10.3%. Wikipedia (7.3%), LinkedIn (6.5%), and Forbes (5.3%) round out the top five off-page sources overall, but individual AI models show distinct preferences beyond this average. Model-specific preferences vary significantly: Reddit represents 51.8% of Grok's off-page citations and 30.4% of Perplexity's, while Copilot leans more heavily on Bing-indexed and retail sources like Amazon (6%) and Walmart (3.2%). Vertical-specific authority sources often outrank the all-segment leaders: in Financial Services, Bankrate (27.9%) and NerdWallet (24.4%) outrank Reddit as top-cited sources, while in Healthcare, PMC/NCBI (10.2%) and Healthline (9%) lead. An effective GEO strategy must expand beyond owned content (blog, homepage, product pages) to include a presence plan for vertical-specific authority sites, since these sources feed directly into how AI models describe a brand. Building an AI visibility strategy requires a clear understanding of how answer engines actually operate, which is why we created the State of AI Search 2026 Report : to share trends we’ve observed from millions of data points spanning 8+ LLMs, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity. However, we also wanted to go deeper and contextualize our findings, turning to extensive conversations with marketers grappling with a whole new acquisition channel that forms its own opinions on which brands or products to recommend. Today, we’re answering one of the biggest questions about off-page signals. Methodology Between December 2025 and March 2026, we collected and analyzed millions of AI-generated responses across B2B and B2C. We also layered the product data with a supplementary analysis of over 500 conversations in Q2 (April-June 2026), including enterprise demos, strategy sessions, and onboarding calls. We identified the most common questions and unresolved priorities for marketing teams building out GEO programs. These companies include both enterprise and mid-market teams, with a median average revenue of $933 million and median average size of 755 employees. Each question in this blog series is answered with benchmark metrics compiled from our product data, along with a series of recommended action items to improve your GEO efforts. You can view the full report here. How Do You Integrate Off-page Signals into Your AI Visibility Strategy? Off-page signals are often the primary source for AI answer engines. Reddit alone accounts for 21.9% of all off-page citations across every AI model we track, more than double the next closest source, YouTube, at 10.3%. Wikipedia (7.3%), LinkedIn (6.5%), and Forbes (5.3%) round out the top five. However, individual models also have particular preferences. For example, Reddit represents 51.8% of Grok's off-page citations and 30.4% of Perplexity's, while Copilot leans more heavily on Bing-indexed and retail sources like Amazon (6%) and Walmart (3.2%). Vertical-specific sources also factor into the equation. In Financial Services, Bankrate (27.9%) and NerdWallet (24.4%) outrank Reddit as the top-cited sources, while in Healthcare, PMC/NCBI (10.2%) and Healthline (9%) lead. What does this mean for marketers? An effective GEO strategy needs to expand its focus beyond owned content like the blog, homepage, and product pages, and factor in vertical-specific authority sites. Action Items Identify the top five off-page sources specific to your vertical (not just the all-segment average) and build a presence plan for each, whether genuine community engagement, contributed expert content, or structured data partnerships. Monitor brand mentions and sentiment on Reddit and the other top platforms in your category as a standing part, since these sources feed directly into how models describe you (even when you have no control over the content itself). If your category has a dominant niche authority site (Bankrate and NerdWallet in finance, Healthline and Mayo Clinic in healthcare, Zillow and Angi in real estate), prioritize earning legitimate placement, citations, or data partnerships over generic PR outreach. For more insights, check out the full State of AI Search 2026 report . FAQs How do you integrate off-page signals into your AI visibility strategy? Off-page signals should be treated as a primary input for AI answer engines, not a secondary channel. This means identifying the top off-page sources specific to your vertical, building a presence plan for each (through community engagement, contributed expert content, or structured data partnerships), and monitoring brand mentions and sentiment on those platforms as a standing practice, since AI models draw directly on them when describing your brand. Which off-page source has the biggest impact on AI citations? Reddit is the single largest off-page source across all AI models tracked, accounting for 21.9% of all off-page citations. That's more than double the next closest source, YouTube, at 10.3%. Wikipedia (7.3%), LinkedIn (6.5%), and Forbes (5.3%) round out the overall top five. Do different AI models rely on different off-page sources? Yes, model-specific preferences diverge significantly from the overall average. Reddit represents 51.8% of Grok's off-page citations and 30.4% of Perplexity's, well above the 21.9% cross-model average. Copilot, by contrast, leans more heavily on Bing-indexed and retail sources, citing Amazon in 6% of cases and Walmart in 3.2%. Does the top off-page source change by industry vertical? Yes. While Reddit leads across the all-segment average, vertical-specific authority sites often outrank it within a given category. In Financial Services, Bankrate (27.9%) and NerdWallet (24.4%) are cited more than Reddit. In Healthcare, PMC/NCBI (10.2%) and Healthline (9%) lead as the top-cited sources. Why can't marketers rely solely on owned content for AI visibility? Because AI answer engines draw heavily on off-page, third-party sources when forming responses, a strategy focused only on owned content like the blog, homepage, and product pages misses the sources that most directly shape how models describe a brand. Off-page signals, particularly community platforms and vertical-specific authority sites, need to be an explicit part of the GEO strategy. How should marketers prioritize which off-page sources to focus on? Marketers should identify the top five off-page sources specific to their own vertical, rather than relying on the all-segment average, and build a presence plan for each. If a category has a dominant niche authority site, such as Bankrate and NerdWallet in finance or Healthline and Mayo Clinic in healthcare, earning legitimate placement or data partnerships with that site should take priority over generic PR outreach. What data supports these off-page citation findings? The findings are based on millions of AI-generated responses collected between December 2025 and March 2026 across B2B and B2C, supplemented by an analysis of over 500 conversations in Q2 2026 (April–June), including enterprise demos, strategy sessions, and onboarding calls with enterprise and mid-market teams averaging $933 million in revenue and 755 employees.

summary: See which RFP response software leads in July 2026 for government proposals, from compliance matrix automation to AI drafting and FedRAMP
body_text: Compliance gaps, disconnected capture data, and last-minute reformatting are usually symptoms of the wrong tool, not the wrong team. General-purpose RFP response software tends to show its limits fast when you're working against Section L/M requirements and a hard submission deadline. Here's how six purpose-built and GovCon-adjacent tools stack up across the dimensions that actually matter for federal proposals. TLDR: Purpose-built GovCon RFP response software handles Section L/M traceability, content reuse, and compliance verification where general tools fall short. Automated compliance matrix generation in Excel separates tools built for federal work from those adapted to it. Native Word integration matters: web-centric tools create version control risk when your final deliverable lives in a Word proposal shell. FedRAMP Moderate Authorized and FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent are not the same designation; the difference affects CUI handling depending on agency and contract type. One purpose-built federal proposal tool in this comparison covers the full capture-to-submission lifecycle with automated compliance matrix generation, AI-assisted drafting, and native Microsoft Suite integration. What Is RFP Response Software? RFP response software manages the full response lifecycle within the structure federal procurements demand: Section L drives what you submit, Section M drives how it scores, and FAR clauses and page limits govern the rest. General tools handle three things poorly: requirement extraction and traceability, content reuse from past proposals, and compliance verification. A missed requirement shows up as a gap at Red Team review or in an evaluation panel's scoring notes. How We Ranked These RFP Response Software Solutions The following criteria separate purpose-built RFP response software from tools that cover only part of the federal proposal workflow: End-to-end lifecycle coverage, from bid/no-bid analysis through color team review, without stitching together disconnected point tools. Microsoft Word and Excel integration depth, since most federal proposal workflows live in those environments regardless of what sits alongside them. Compliance matrix output format: whether Section L/M extraction outputs to Excel natively without manual reformatting. CUI handling and security posture, including FedRAMP status and GCC/GCC High support, which vary across tools and affect which contracts a solution can support. Capture-to-proposal continuity: whether capture intelligence reaches the proposal workspace or stays siloed in a CRM. A Leading RFP Response Software for Federal Proposals: GovEagle GovEagle is built exclusively for government contractors, covering the full capture-to-submission workflow. The compliance matrix generation alone separates it from the broader category: GovEagle reads the RFP, extracts every Section L requirement, and produces the matrix in Excel automatically, eliminating the manual extraction work that typically consumes the first day of any pursuit. What GovEagle Does GovEagle operates across the full proposal lifecycle, from pre-RFP opportunity intelligence through final submission. Key capabilities include: Automated compliance matrix generation in Excel, cross-referenced against Section L and Section M evaluation factors so nothing gets missed in the shred process. AI-assisted first drafts generated from your past performance library, prior proposals, and uploaded source materials, writers refine from a populated draft, not a blank document. Native Sharepoint, Microsoft Word and Excel integration, with built-in color team review workflows, so the tool fits into how proposal teams already work. Security and Compliance Posture GovEagle runs on AWS GovCloud with FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent controls, CMMC Level 2 support, and NIST 800-171 alignment, with GCC/GCC High deployment options for teams handling CUI. Teams handling CUI should verify their tool's deployment environment aligns with applicable security requirements for their contract and agency context. Documented Results Precise Software used GovEagle on early-stage proposals and cut SME time by 80 percent, freeing subject matter experts for technical solutioning instead of document assembly. GovDash GovDash combines AI-assisted proposal drafting, opportunity tracking, compliance matrices, content management, and pursuit tracking in one platform. It reports FedRAMP Moderate Equivalency and FedRAMP Ready status; organizations handling CUI should confirm alignment with contract requirements. Best suited for mid-size GovCon firms seeking a unified BD and proposal management workflow. Trade-offs to Consider GovDash supports a Microsoft Word add-in and integrations with Excel and PowerPoint, although teams should compare the depth of its in-document workflow, content governance, and repository controls against their specific requirements. GovSignals GovSignals is an intelligence and proposal generation tool for government contractors, pulling opportunity data from SAM.gov contract opportunities and other federal sources to help teams draft proposal sections, build compliance matrices, and track pursuit pipelines. Where Teams Run Into Friction The workflow narrows once a pursuit moves into active proposal development: GovSignals is primarily browser-based, which creates friction for teams whose drafting workflows live in Microsoft Word and Excel. Moving content between the tool and familiar proposal artifacts adds steps to an already compressed timeline. Compliance matrix generation exists within the tool, but teams working across large, multi-volume RFPs often find they need to export and reformat outputs to match agency-specified deliverable structures. pWin.ai pWin.ai targets capture managers and proposal teams with automated bid/no-bid scoring, compliance tracking, and draft generation. Its scoring models pull from federal procurement data to help BD shops triage opportunities. Proposal generation leans on templated outputs that often require substantial manual rework to meet Section L/M requirements, making it better suited as a capture intelligence layer than a full response engine for complex, multi-volume submissions. pWin.ai states that it integrates with Microsoft Word, Excel, and SharePoint, allowing teams to fold the platform into existing Microsoft-based proposal workflows. Buyers should compare the depth and usability of those integrations against their specific workflow requirements. AskSage AskSage is a cloud-based AI assistant for federal agencies and cleared contractors, with deployments across classification levels including SECRET and TOP SECRET. It is built around secure AI access, not proposal workflow automation. For teams on highly classified programs where standard SaaS tools are off the table, AskSage fills a real gap, supporting document analysis, content drafting, and solicitation querying against uploaded materials within secure environments. Where AskSage Fits in the Proposal Context AskSage handles general document interaction and content generation, but it was not purpose-built around federal proposal mechanics. Teams looking for compliance matrix generation, Section L/M traceability, or structured RFP response workflows will likely need to build those processes around the tool; those workflows do not come ready to use. VisibleThread VisibleThread combines deterministic compliance analysis with generative AI capabilities for proposal drafting, document refinement, readability review, and requirement traceability. Its current platform includes automated compliance-matrix generation, Microsoft Word-based drafting support, and proposal-management workflows alongside its proven document-analysis capabilities. What VisibleThread Does Well Proposal managers working under tight pink, red, and gold team review timelines often find value in VisibleThread's document analysis capabilities. The tool can parse Section L and Section M requirements, cross-reference them against draft content, and surface where responses fall short before a color team review catches the gap. Compliance gap analysis against solicitation requirements, with traceable line-by-line cross-referencing that gives reviewers a clear audit trail in place of a subjective read Readability scoring calibrated to federal evaluation standards, which matters when evaluators are scoring under time pressure and dense prose creates unnecessary risk Trade-offs to Consider Its workflow positioning remains the primary trade-off. Although the platform has expanded beyond post-draft review to include AI-assisted drafting, automated compliance-matrix creation, Microsoft Word integration, and broader proposal-management capabilities. Teams should still compare its pre-RFP capture functionality and end-to-end workflow coverage with platforms built squarely around the full capture-to-submission lifecycle. For teams looking for a single tool that covers capture through submission, it is a meaningful constraint. RFP Response Software Feature Comparison Table Choosing the right RFP response software comes down to how well a tool fits into your actual proposal workflow, beyond its feature count. The table below maps the six solutions covered in this post across the dimensions that matter most to GovCon pursuit teams: AI drafting capability, compliance matrix generation, Microsoft Word integration, security posture, and pricing structure. Before a single section is drafted, GovEagle generates the compliance matrix in Excel and the annotated outline in Word, giving proposal managers a requirement-mapped structure tied directly to Section L and Section M. GovEagle stands apart by generating both an Excel compliance matrix and a Word annotated outline before drafting begins.From there, coverage runs the full pursuit lifecycle: bid/no-bid analysis, AI-assisted drafting across technical, management, and past performance volumes, and automated color team review, all within the Microsoft Suite. Salesforce, Unanet CRM, SharePoint, and existing content repositories connect without data migration, so capture intelligence already in your CRM flows directly into the proposal workflow.For teams handling CUI, the security architecture holds up to GovCon scrutiny. GovEagle operates at FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent controls with NIST 800-171 alignment, CMMC support, and GCC/GCC High deployment options, giving security reviewers a documented posture without requiring a separate environment for sensitive content. FAQs How do I choose between GovEagle, GovDash, GovSignals, pWin.ai, and AskSage for my federal proposal workflow? Start by identifying where your workflow breaks down most often: if compliance matrix generation and end-to-end lifecycle coverage are the bottleneck, GovEagle or GovDash are the strongest fits; if pre-solicitation intelligence and capture analysis are the priority, GovSignals or pWin.ai cover that ground; if your constraint is secure AI access at classification level, AskSage fills that specific gap. Teams pursuing complex, multi-volume federal RFPs with Section L/M requirements will find purpose-built GovCon tools outperform general-purpose or capture-only options at the drafting and compliance stages. Is GovEagle better than GovDash for teams that draft proposals in Microsoft Word? GovEagle offers a native Word add-in that keeps proposal teams inside their existing drafting environment, with compliance matrix output generated directly in Excel. GovDash's drafting workflow is more web-centric, which can introduce formatting and version control friction when the final deliverable needs to land in a Word-formatted proposal shell. Teams whose entire submission workflow lives in Microsoft Office documents will typically find GovEagle's integration depth reduces handoff steps that GovDash requires. What security posture should I verify before deploying any RFP response software for CUI-handling proposals? Security requirements such as FedRAMP authorization for applicable federal cloud use and NIST SP 800-171 controls for nonfederal systems that process, store, or transmit CUI may apply depending on the agency, contract, and deployment context. Verify the tool's environment against the specific contractual requirements before procurement. FedRAMP Moderate Authorized and FedRAMP Moderate Equivalent are distinct designations, and neither should be assumed interchangeable when your contract or agency context involves CUI. Final Thoughts on Picking RFP Response Software That Fits Federal Work The right RFP response software for federal work comes down to three filters: how well it handles Section L/M traceability, whether it fits your existing Microsoft Office workflow, and whether its security posture holds up under agency review. For teams pursuing structured federal RFPs at meaningful volume, GovEagle covers the full capture-to-submission lifecycle, from automated compliance matrix generation in Excel through AI-assisted drafting and color team review, without requiring teams to leave the Microsoft Suite.

title: Nine Wynn Restaurants Clinch Wine Spectator 2026 "Best of Award of Excellence"
summary: Macao, July 8, 2026 — Nine signature restaurants across Wynn Palace and Wynn Macau have been awarded the prestigious
body_text: Macao, July 8, 2026 — Nine signature restaurants across Wynn Palace and Wynn Macau have been awarded the prestigious "Best of Award of Excellence" at the Wine Spectator 2026 Restaurant Awards. The awarded establishments include Chef Tam's Seasons, Lakeview Palace, Mizumi, Sushi Mizumi, SW Steakhouse, and Sole e Mare at Fontana at Wynn Palace, alongside Wing Lei, Drunken Fish, and Lakeside Trattoria at Wynn Macau. This international recognition underscores Wynn's continuous pursuit of exceptional dining experiences and its dedication to the art of wine pairing. It further highlights Wynn's expertise in wine list curation and professional sommelier services, while reflecting its steadfast commitment to promoting Chinese wines globally through its "Wynn Signature Chinese Wine Awards" program. Together, these efforts reinforce Macao's reputation as a UNESCO "Creative City of Gastronomy". Wine program highlights across nine award-winning restaurants The wine programs across the winning restaurants at Wynn complement an exceptional range of cuisines. For Chinese cuisine, Wing Lei , the MICHELIN Two-Star Cantonese restaurant at Wynn Macau, pairs classic Cantonese fare with a wine list rich in diverse vintages and regions. At Wynn Palace, Chef Tam's Seasons , which holds two MICHELIN stars and is recognized among Asia's 50 Best Restaurants, complements its seasonal menus inspired by 24 solar terms with Chinese Baijiu and premium wines, while the wine selection at the modern Jiangnan restaurant Lakeview Palace is tailor-made for the delicate flavor profiles of its signature dishes rooted in the confluence of Huaiyang and Cantonese culinary traditions. Drunken Fish , Wynn Macau's seafood concept that features the city's first Moutai-themed bar, boasts an extensive wine collection alongside rare Moutai expressions to deliver exceptional pairings of Chinese spirits with premium seafood. Complementing their refined Japanese culinary offerings, the MICHELIN One-Star Mizumi and the omakase destination Sushi Mizumi at Wynn Palace present an extraordinary beverage collection featuring exclusive award-winning bottles, seasonal releases, and limited-edition sake from Japan's legendary breweries. Backed by its outstanding sake portfolio, Mizumi's exceptional wine list continues to garner top-tier industry acclaim, notably clinching the "China's Best Sake List" award at the China Wine List of the Year Awards last year. On the Western dining front, SW Steakhouse , the classic American steakhouse at Wynn Palace, anchors its program with iconic American vintages and world-renowned estate collections, complemented by a rare whisky collection. Meanwhile, Wynn's two Italian restaurants – Lakeside Trattoria at Wynn Macau and Sole e Mare at Fontana at Wynn Palace – showcase rich regional Italian wines and international selections, perfectly accentuating the vibrant flavors of authentic Italian delicacies. Award-winning labels from the "Wynn Signature Chinese Wine Awards" enrich Wynn's globally curated wine program Wynn continues to shape the global gastronomy scene by leveraging its hospitality platform to introduce new dimensions to fine dining, presenting exceptional terroirs and emerging wine regions to guests. Through hosting the "Wynn Signature Chinese Wine Awards" for three consecutive years, top-tier Chinese wines – celebrated by international judging panels for capturing the essence of local terroirs – have been incorporated into the wine lists of Wynn's dining establishments, including all nine Wine Spectator award-winning restaurants. The inclusion of these acclaimed Chinese wines further enriches Wynn's beverage portfolio and demonstrates the immense potential of Chinese wines in high-end dining. Furthermore, the competition features the "Wynn Sommelier's Choice" award, where Wynn's sommelier teams meticulously select an award-winning Chinese wine that best complements each restaurant's signature culinary style. This initiative highlights the precision and expertise of Wynn's professional sommelier teams in wine pairing and reflects Wynn's ongoing commitment to advancing pairing excellence across diverse culinary traditions. Established in 1981, the Wine Spectator Restaurant Awards are presented by the globally influential wine publication Wine Spectator, serving as one of the most authoritative grading systems for restaurant wine lists in the industry. The awards feature three tiers: the Award of Excellence, the Best of Award of Excellence, and the Grand Award. The "Best of Award of Excellence" specifically recognizes restaurants that guide wine lovers with lists of significant vintage depth, excellent regional diversity, and a broad selection of top-tier producers. Winning restaurants typically boast 350 or more selections and present them with professional and meticulous lists. Wynn's sweep of awards across nine establishments demonstrates its outstanding strength in fine dining, sommelier expertise, and the art of wine pairing. To taste the delicacies and wine pairings of each award-winning restaurant, guests are welcome to contact the reservation hotlines: (853) 8889 3663 (Wynn Palace) / (853) 8986 3663 (Wynn Macau).

title: Klarna now available on Fragrance.com, bringing flexible payments to one of America's largest online beauty destinations | Klarna International
body_text: New York, July 15, 2026 - Klarna, the global digital bank and flexible payments provider, is now available at checkout on Fragrance.com, a beauty destination with over 40,000 products across fragrances, skincare, makeup, haircare, and candles. The integration is powered by Adyen. Fragrance and beauty purchases are considered, often personal: shoppers research, compare, and return to the same brands season after season. Through this new partnership, Klarna gives Fragrance.com customers the flexibility to split purchases into four interest-free installments, finance larger orders, and earn cashback on qualifying purchases. "Fragrance.com has spent nearly three decades making premium beauty accessible, and that mission aligns with everything Klarna stands for," said David Sykes, Chief Commercial Officer at Klarna. "Beauty shoppers are loyal and intentional, they deserve payment options that match how they actually shop. We're proud to bring Klarna’s flexible payment options to one of the category's most trusted retailers." "We're constantly looking at where we can remove friction, in discovery, in browsing, and at checkout,” said Michael Nadboy, Chief Marketing Officer at Fragrance.com. “Our customers deserve an end-to-end experience that feels effortless, and offering Klarna is strengthening that experience, helping us to ensure every touchpoint lives up to the products we carry."
